core.appStarted.description: Runs once each time Cuebot finishes starting up. Good for setting your variables, switching a scene or saying hello every time you open Cuebot.

core.cron.description: Runs on a clock schedule that you write, like every 15 minutes or every day at 8 pm. It uses your computer's local time and is separate from the Timers page.

fields.expression: Five parts with spaces between: minute, hour, day of the month, month, day of the week. A * means every. "*/15 * * * *" is every 15 minutes, "0 20 * * *" is every day at 20:00.

variables.triggeredAt: The date and time (to the minute) when it ran

core.timer.description: Runs each time one of your timers goes off. You make timers on the Timers page. Good for a repeating reminder like "follow the channel" every 20 minutes.

fields.timer: The name of the timer, exactly as it is on the Timers page, like "Social links". If you leave this empty the action never runs.

variables.timerName: The name of the timer that went off
variables.interval: How many seconds the timer waits between runs
variables.chatLines: How many chat messages came in since the timer last ran

variables.globalCreated.description: Runs when a global variable is saved for the very first time. Global variables are values Cuebot remembers for all actions, like a death counter.

fields.variable: The variable's name without the ~ signs, like "deaths". Empty means any variable.
fields.persisted: Either = both kinds. Yes = only variables that are kept after a restart. No = only temporary ones that vanish when Cuebot closes.

variables.persisted: Whether it is kept after a restart (true or false)

variables.globalUpdated.description: Runs when the value of an existing global variable changes. Handy to react to a counter, like a message when the death counter reaches a new number.

fields.variable: The variable's name without the ~ signs, like "deaths". Empty means any variable.
fields.persisted: Either = both kinds. Yes = only variables that are kept after a restart. No = only temporary ones that vanish when Cuebot closes.

variables.persisted: Whether it is kept after a restart (true or false)

variables.globalDeleted.description: Runs when a global variable is deleted. Be careful with actions that delete the same variable they are listening for.

fields.variable: The variable's name without the ~ signs, like "deaths". Empty means any variable.
fields.persisted: Either = both kinds. Yes = only variables that are kept after a restart. No = only temporary ones that vanish when Cuebot closes.

variables.variableName: The name of the variable that was deleted
variables.persisted: Whether it was a kept variable (true or false)

variables.userUpdated.description: Runs when a variable that belongs to one viewer changes, like their lucky number or their quiz score. Careful: an action that changes the same variable can run itself again.

fields.variable: The variable's name, like "score". Empty means any variable.
fields.persisted: Either = both kinds. Yes = only variables that are kept after a restart. No = only temporary ones.
fields.userLogin: Only react to this viewer, typed like their chat name, for example "kris". Empty means any viewer.
fields.platform: Only react to viewers on this site, like twitch, youtube, kick or rumble. Empty means any.

variables.userId: The viewer's id on their platform
variables.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch

desktop.clipboardChanged.description: Runs when the text you copied (Ctrl+C) changes. You must switch on "Watch clipboard" on the Hotkeys page first, or it never runs.

fields.contains: Only run when the copied text has this in it, like "https://". Empty means any copied text.

variables.clipboardText: The text that was just copied

core.fileChanged.description: Runs when a file in a folder you watch is changed. You set up what to watch on the Watchers page. Good for reacting to a text file another program writes.

fields.watcher: The name of a folder watcher from the Watchers page. Empty means every watcher.

variables.filePath: The full location of the file on your computer
variables.folder: The folder the file is in
variables.fileSize: How big the file is, in bytes (small text files only)
variables.lineCount: How many lines the file has (small text files only)
variables.line0: The first line of the file (line1 is the second, and so on)
variables.watcherName: The name of the watcher that noticed

core.fileCreated.description: Runs when a new file appears in a folder you watch. You set up what to watch on the Watchers page. Good for reacting to a new screenshot or recording.

fields.watcher: The name of a folder watcher from the Watchers page. Empty means every watcher.

variables.filePath: The full location of the file on your computer
variables.folder: The folder the file is in
variables.watcherName: The name of the watcher that noticed

core.fileDeleted.description: Runs when a file is deleted from a folder you watch. You set up what to watch on the Watchers page.

fields.watcher: The name of a folder watcher from the Watchers page. Empty means every watcher.

variables.filePath: The full location the file had
variables.folder: The folder the file was in
variables.watcherName: The name of the watcher that noticed

core.fileRenamed.description: Runs when a file in a folder you watch gets a new name. You set up what to watch on the Watchers page.

fields.watcher: The name of a folder watcher from the Watchers page. Empty means every watcher.

variables.fileName: The new name of the file
variables.filePath: The full new location of the file
variables.oldFilePath: The full old location of the file
variables.watcherName: The name of the watcher that noticed

core.fileTailLine.description: Runs for each new line that a program adds to the end of a text file you follow, like a game's log. You choose the file on the Watchers page.

fields.watcher: The name of a file tail from the Watchers page. Empty means every file tail.

variables.filePath: The full location of the file
variables.watcherName: The name of the file tail that noticed

hotkeys.pressed.description: Runs when you press a keyboard shortcut. You make shortcuts on the Hotkeys page, or you can type a combination like Ctrl+Shift+F1 here.

fields.hotkey: A hotkey name from the Hotkeys page, or keys like "Ctrl+Shift+F1". Empty means any hotkey.

variables.hotkeyName: The name of the hotkey from the Hotkeys page
variables.hotkey: The keys that were pressed, like Ctrl+Shift+F1

input.mouseClick.description: Runs when you click a mouse button anywhere on your computer. It does not work on Wayland (a Linux desktop type), because that blocks other programs from seeing clicks.

fields.button: Which mouse button counts. Any means all of them. X1 and X2 are the extra side buttons.
fields.modifiers: Keys that must be held while clicking, like "Ctrl+Shift". Empty = does not matter. "None" = no key held. Otherwise exactly the keys you list.

variables.mouseButton: Which button was clicked, like Left
variables.mouseX: How far from the left of the screen the click was, in pixels
variables.mouseY: How far from the top of the screen the click was, in pixels
variables.modifiers: Which keys were held during the click, like Ctrl+Shift

core.processStarted.description: Runs when a program you watch starts on your computer, like your game. You choose which programs to watch on the Watchers page.

fields.watcher: The name of a process watcher from the Watchers page. Empty means every process watcher.

variables.processName: The name of the program that started
variables.processId: The number the computer gave this running program
variables.path: The folder the program lives in (when Cuebot can find it)
variables.watcherName: The name of the watcher that noticed

core.processStopped.description: Runs when a program you watch closes, like your game. You choose which programs to watch on the Watchers page.

fields.watcher: The name of a process watcher from the Watchers page. Empty means every process watcher.

variables.processName: The name of the program that closed
variables.processId: The number the computer had given this program
variables.watcherName: The name of the watcher that noticed

desktop.toastActivated.description: Runs when you click a pop-up notification that Cuebot showed with "Show desktop notification". Handy for a notification that acts like a button.

fields.toastId: The notification id you typed in "Show desktop notification", like "raid-alert". Empty means any notification.

variables.toastId: The id of the notification you clicked
variables.toastTitle: The title shown on the notification
variables.toastMessage: The message shown on the notification

groups.added.description: Runs when a new, empty group of viewers is created. Groups are lists of viewers, like "Trusted", made on the Users & Groups page or with an action.

fields.group: The group's name. Empty means any group.

groups.removed.description: Runs when a group of viewers is deleted.

fields.group: The group's name. Empty means any group.

groups.cleared.description: Runs when every viewer is taken out of a group at once, but the group itself stays.

fields.group: The group's name. Empty means any group.

variables.count: How many viewers were taken out

groups.usersAdded.description: Runs when a viewer is put into a group. Good for welcoming someone to "VIPs" or "Trusted".

fields.group: The group's name. Empty means any group.

variables.userId: The viewer's id on their platform
variables.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch

groups.usersRemoved.description: Runs when a viewer is taken out of a group.

fields.group: The group's name. Empty means any group.

variables.userId: The viewer's id on their platform
variables.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch

users.firstWords.description: Runs when a viewer writes in chat for the first time of the stream. Great for a welcome message. It starts over each time you go live, or when you reset it.

fields.platform: Only react to chat on this site. All means every site you are connected to.

variables.platform: The site they wrote on, like twitch
variables.isNewUser: True if this is the first time Cuebot has ever seen them
variables.messageCount: How many messages Cuebot has seen from them in total

users.presentViewers.description: Runs every few minutes with the viewers who chatted recently. Good for giving points to everyone who is around. Set how often on the Users & Groups page.

fields.platform: Only react to viewers on this site. All means every site you are connected to.

variables.platform: The site these viewers are on
variables.userNames: Their names in one line, separated by commas
variables.userIds: Their ids in one line, separated by commas
variables.isLive: Whether the stream is live, when the site tells Cuebot

command.triggered.description: Runs when a viewer uses one of your chat commands, like !hello. You make commands on the Commands page. This trigger lets any action react to a command.

fields.command: The command's name from the Commands page. Empty means every command.

variables.user: The viewer who used the command
variables.rawInput: Only the text after the command, like "kris 50" in "!give kris 50"
variables.input0: The first word after the command (input1 is the second, and so on)
variables.inputCount: How many words came after the command
variables.counter: How many times this command has been used
variables.userCounter: How many times this viewer has used it
variables.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch

command.cooldown.description: Runs when a viewer tries a command that is still cooling down, so it did not run. Good for a friendly reply like "wait 30 more seconds". The broadcaster is never blocked.

fields.command: The command's name from the Commands page. Empty means every command.

variables.user: The viewer who tried the command
variables.remaining: How many seconds are left before it works again
variables.cooldownType: Whether the wait is for everyone (Global) or just this viewer (User)
variables.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch

core.clearActionQueue.description: Throws away the actions waiting in line in an action queue. Actions already running finish. Handy as an "emergency stop" button for a pile-up of alerts.

fields.queue: The name of a queue from the Queues page, or All for every queue.

variables.queueCleared: How many waiting runs were thrown away

core.comment.description: A note to yourself in the list of steps. It does nothing when the action runs. Good for explaining what a part of a long action is for.

fields.color: A color for the note in the editor, like #E0A030. Empty uses the normal color. It only changes how it looks.

core.delay.description: Waits before moving to the next step. 1000 milliseconds is 1 second. Good between a sound and a scene switch. It can also wait a random time.

fields.milliseconds: How long to wait, in milliseconds. 1000 = 1 second, 5000 = 5 seconds.
fields.random: Tick to wait a random time between the first number and the "To" number, instead of always the same time.
fields.to: The longest wait, in milliseconds, when "Random delay" is ticked. With 1000 and 3000 it waits 1 to 3 seconds. Not used if unticked.

core.getActionGroupState.description: Checks an action group and tells you if all, none or some of its actions are turned on. The group is the "Group" box in an action's settings.

fields.group: The group's name, as shown in your Actions list, like "Alerts".

variables.actionGroupState: 0 = all are off, 1 = all are on, 2 = some on and some off
variables.actionsEnabled: A list with the ids of the actions that are on
variables.actionsDisabled: A list with the ids of the actions that are off

core.getActionState.description: Finds out whether an action is turned on or off and keeps the answer in a variable. Pair it with an If step to act on the answer.

fields.action: The action's name, exactly as in your Actions list.
fields.name: The variable that receives the answer (true = on, false = off), without % signs. The default is actionEnabled.

variables.actionState: True if the action is on, false if it is off

core.group.description: A folder for steps. Keeps a long action tidy. It can also run just ONE random step from inside, like picking one of five different thank-you messages.

fields.name: A name for the group so you can see what is inside, like "Greetings". Only for you.
fields.random: Tick to run only ONE step inside, picked at random, instead of all of them. Each step's weight makes it more or less likely.
fields.color: A color for the group in the editor, like #3A7BD5. Empty uses the normal color. It only changes how it looks.

core.sendSignal.description: Sends a secret message to other actions that are waiting with "Wait for local signal", which wakes them up. Handy to make one action wait for another.

fields.name: A name you make up, like "go". The waiting step must use exactly the same name.
fields.includeArgs: Tick to also hand over this action's %variables% to the action that wakes up.
fields.arguments: Extra variables to hand over, one per line as name=value. Example: winner=%user%
fields.queue: Tick to keep the signal if nobody is waiting yet, so the next wait gets it. Unticked, it is lost if nobody is waiting.

variables.signalWaiters: How many waiting actions were woken up

core.setActionGroupState.description: Turns every action in an action group on or off, or flips each one. Handy to switch a whole set on together, like all your giveaway actions.

fields.group: The group's name, as shown in your Actions list, like "Alerts".
fields.state: Enable turns them on. Disable turns them off. Toggle flips each action to its opposite.

core.setActionQueueBlocking.description: Switches the "blocking" option of an action queue. A blocking queue runs one action at a time, so the others wait their turn. The change is saved.

fields.queue: The name of a queue from the Queues page. The Default queue cannot be changed.
fields.state: Enable = blocking on (one at a time). Disable = off (actions may overlap). Toggle = switch to the opposite.

core.setActionQueuePause.description: Pauses or resumes an action queue. While paused, actions wait in line instead of running. Good for holding alerts back during a serious moment.

fields.queue: The name of a queue from the Queues page, or All for every queue.
fields.state: Pause holds actions back. Resume lets them run again. Toggle switches to the opposite.
fields.clear: Tick to also throw away the actions already waiting in line.

core.setActionState.description: Turns another action on or off, or flips it. A turned-off action ignores its triggers. Good for "only allow this while a giveaway runs". The change is saved.

fields.action: The action's name, exactly as in your Actions list.
fields.state: Enable turns it on. Disable turns it off. Toggle switches it to the opposite.

core.setSubActionState.description: Turns one single step of an action on or off, without opening the editor. A turned-off step is skipped when the action runs. The change is saved.

fields.action: The action's name, exactly as in your Actions list.
fields.subAction: Which step: its number in the action (1 = the first; steps inside groups and branches are counted too) or its id.
fields.state: Enable turns it on. Disable turns it off. Toggle switches it to the opposite.

core.setSubActionWeight.description: Changes how likely a step is to be picked when an action or group runs one random step. A bigger weight is picked more often. The change is saved.

fields.action: The action's name, exactly as in your Actions list.
fields.subAction: Which step: its number in the action (1 = the first; steps inside groups and branches are counted too) or its id.
fields.weight: How likely it is compared with the other steps. With weights 1 and 3, the second is picked three times as often. 0 = never.

core.setTriggerState.description: Turns one trigger of an action on or off, without opening the editor. A turned-off trigger no longer starts the action. The change is saved.

fields.action: The action's name, exactly as in your Actions list.
fields.trigger: Which trigger: its number in the action's trigger list (1 = the first), its id, or its type name.
fields.state: Enable turns it on. Disable turns it off. Toggle switches it to the opposite.

core.triggerCustomEvent.description: Sends out a custom event with a name you choose. Any action with a matching "Custom code event" trigger runs. A way to start several actions at once.

fields.eventName: A name you make up, like "party-time". The action that should run needs a Custom code event trigger with the same name.
fields.useArgs: Tick to hand over this action's %variables% to the actions that start.

core.waitForSignal.description: Pauses this action until another action sends the same signal. Good for waiting on a button press before going on. It can give up after a time limit.

fields.name: The signal's name, exactly as in "Send local signal", like "go".
fields.timeoutMs: How long to wait before giving up, in milliseconds. 1000 = 1 second. 0 = wait forever.
fields.stopOnTimeout: Tick to stop the whole action if the wait runs out. Unticked, the action carries on with the next step.
fields.overwrite: Tick so variables sent with the signal replace this action's variables with the same name. Unticked, yours are kept.

variables.signalTimeout: True if the wait ran out first
variables.signalName: The name of the signal that arrived
variables.hasResult: True if the signal brought variables with it

core.log.description: Writes a line in Cuebot's log, which you can read to see what your actions do. Great for checking a %variable% while testing. Viewers never see it.

fields.message: The text to write. You can use %variables%, like "Raid from %user%".
fields.level: How important it is: Debug (tiny detail), Info (normal), Warning (something odd), Error (something broke).

core.getInputDialog.description: Opens a small window on your computer asking you to type something, then saves your answer in a variable. Handy for actions you start yourself, like asking for a new title.

fields.title: The text at the top of the window. The default is Cuebot.
fields.prompt: The question shown in the window, like "Which game next?".
fields.originalText: Text already in the box when the window opens. Empty = an empty box.
fields.variable: The variable that receives your answer, without % signs. The default inputResult means you use %inputResult% later.
fields.autoType: Tick so a number you type is saved as a real number and not just text. Untick if unsure.

variables.success: True if you pressed OK, false if you cancelled or no window could open
variables.inputResult: What you typed (the variable name can be changed in the settings)

core.if.description: Checks something, then runs different steps depending on the answer. Example: IF %message% contains "hello" THEN say hi back. Steps go under True (yes) or False (no).

fields.left: The thing to look at, usually a %variable% like %user% or %message%. For "exists" and "does not exist" type only the variable's name, like targetUser.
fields.operator: How to compare. "equals" = the same. "contains" = has it inside. "greater than" and "less than" compare numbers. "is empty" = nothing there. "matches regex" is an advanced search pattern.
fields.right: What to compare with, like hello or 100. Capital letters do not matter. Not used for "is empty", "is not empty", "exists" and "does not exist".

variables.match.count: Only with "matches regex": how many pieces matched
variables.match[0]: Only with "matches regex": the text that matched (match[1] is the first captured piece)

core.loopBreak.description: Stops the loop you are in right now and carries on with the step after the loop. Use it inside a While loop. Outside a loop it stops the whole action.

core.loopContinue.description: Skips the rest of this round of the loop and starts the next round straight away. Use it inside a While loop. Outside a loop it stops the whole action.

core.runAction.description: Runs another action from this one, like calling a helper. Good for reusing the same steps in many actions. The other action gets a copy of this action's variables.

fields.action: The other action's name, exactly as in your Actions list, like "Play alert sound". A wrong name gives an error.
fields.wait: Ticked: this action waits until the other one is done before the next step. Unticked: both run at the same time.

core.getInput.description: Cuts a text into pieces and gives each piece its own variable: %input0%, %input1% and so on. Handy for chat like "!give kris 50".

fields.input: The text to cut up. The default %rawInput% is what a viewer typed after a command.
fields.separator: What to cut at, like a comma. Empty cuts at spaces.

variables.input0: The first piece (input1 is the second, and so on)

core.stop.description: Stops this action right here. The steps below it do not run. Usually put inside an If, like "if the viewer has too few points, stop".

core.switch.description: Like several Ifs in one. It looks at one value and runs the steps of the first case that matches. Example: !color red or blue or green. "Default" runs if nothing matches.

fields.input: The value to look at, usually a %variable% like %message% or %input0%.
fields.cases: One case per line, like red. Put several words on one line with | between them (red|crimson) for the same steps. The first match wins.
fields.operator: How each case is compared with the value: "equals" = the same, "contains" = has it inside, and so on. Capital letters do not matter.

variables.switchCase: The case line that matched, or Default

core.while.description: Repeats the steps inside as long as a check is true, like "while the count is below 5, do this". Handy for doing something several times. It has a safety limit.

fields.left: The thing to look at each round, usually a %variable%. The default %loopIteration% counts rounds starting at 0.
fields.operator: How to compare, like "less than" or "equals". "less than" with 10 repeats while the value is below 10.
fields.right: What to compare with, like 10. The default repeats 10 times (rounds 0 to 9).
fields.maxIterations: The most rounds allowed, so a mistake can never loop forever. 0 = no limit (risky).

variables.loopIteration: Which round you are on, starting at 0

core.clearTemporaryGlobals.description: Deletes all global variables that are not kept after a restart. Variables you kept are not touched. Good for a fresh start at the beginning of a stream.

core.clearTemporaryUserVariables.description: Deletes the viewer variables that are not kept after a restart, for everyone. Kept ones stay. Good for a fresh start, like resetting a quiz.

fields.platform: Only clear for viewers on this site, like twitch. Empty = all sites.

core.deleteGlobal.description: Deletes a global variable, so it is gone. Good to reset something like a counter completely.

fields.name: The variable's name without the ~ signs, like "deaths".

core.deleteUserVariable.description: Deletes a variable that belongs to one viewer, or to every viewer. Good to reset something like a quiz score.

fields.name: The variable's name, like "score".
fields.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch. Empty = the site of whoever started the action.
fields.userId: The viewer's id on their site. Empty = the viewer who started the action, or the one found by user name.
fields.userName: The viewer's chat name, like "kris". Used to find the viewer when you give no id.
fields.allUsers: Tick to delete it from every viewer of that site (all sites if Platform is empty), not just one.

core.getGlobal.description: Reads a global variable and puts its value in a normal variable you can use with %name%. Needed when you want to check a remembered value, like a death count.

fields.name: The global variable's name without the ~ signs, like "deaths".
fields.destination: The variable that receives the value, without % signs. Empty = same name as the global variable.
fields.defaultValue: The value to use if the global variable does not exist yet. Empty = leave the variable unset.
fields.autoType: Tick so numbers stay real numbers (needed for greater/less than checks). Normally leave it ticked.

core.getUserVariable.description: Reads a variable that belongs to one viewer, like their score, and puts the value in a normal variable you can use with %name%.

fields.name: The viewer variable's name, like "score".
fields.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch. Empty = the site of whoever started the action.
fields.userId: The viewer's id on their site. Empty = the viewer who started the action, or the one found by user name.
fields.userName: The viewer's chat name, like "kris". Used to find the viewer when you give no id.
fields.destination: The variable that receives the value, without % signs. Empty = same name as the viewer variable.
fields.defaultValue: The value to use if the viewer or variable does not exist. Empty = leave the variable unset.
fields.autoType: Tick so numbers stay real numbers (needed for greater/less than checks). Normally leave it ticked.

core.pickColor.description: Picks a color and saves it in several formats for other steps, like OBS or a light. Pick the color while editing, run it, then use %color.html% and friends.

fields.color: The color as hex digits: #RRGGBB, like #FF9146, or #AARRGGBB when you want see-through (alpha).
fields.name: A name for the result variables, without %. With "color" you get %color.html% and the others.

variables.color.html: The color as #RRGGBB (name is the one you chose)
variables.color.obs: The color as a number in the format OBS expects
variables.color.color.r: The red part, 0 to 255 (g = green, b = blue, a = see-through)

core.randomNumber.description: Picks a random number, like rolling a dice, and saves it in a variable. Good for "roll 1 to 100" commands or a chance for something to happen.

fields.type: Between = a whole number from Minimum to Maximum. Next Float = a number from 0 to 1, plus a percent from 0 to 100.
fields.name: The variable that gets the number, without % signs. Default random means you use %random%. Only for Between.
fields.min: The lowest number that can be picked, like 1.
fields.max: The highest number that can be picked, like 100. This number can be picked too.

variables.random: The number that was picked (the variable name can be changed)
variables.randomFloat: Only with Next Float: a number from 0 up to just below 1
variables.randomPercent: Only with Next Float: the same as a whole percent, 0 to 100

core.setArgument.description: Creates a variable for this run only, or changes it. Use it afterwards as %name%. Good for building a message or counting inside one action.

fields.name: The variable's name without % signs, like "greeting". Use it later as %greeting%.
fields.value: What to store. You can mix %variables%, ~global variables~ and math like $math(%count% + 1)$.
fields.autoType: Tick so numbers and true/false are stored as real numbers/yes-no values and not plain text. Needed for greater/less than checks.

core.setGlobal.description: Saves a value that every action can read later as ~name~, like a death counter. It can set it or count up and down. Kept after a restart by default.

fields.name: The variable's name, like "deaths". Use it anywhere as ~deaths~.
fields.mode: Value = save exactly what you type. Increment = add to the current number. Decrement = subtract from it.
fields.value: With Value: what to save. With Increment/Decrement: how much to add or subtract (empty = 1).
fields.persisted: Tick to keep it after Cuebot restarts. Untick for a temporary value that vanishes when Cuebot closes.
fields.autoType: Tick so numbers and true/false are stored as real numbers/yes-no values and not plain text.
fields.storeIn: Optional. A variable to also receive the new value, without % signs, so you can use %name% in the next steps.

core.setUserVariable.description: Saves a value that belongs to one viewer, like their score or favorite color. It can set it or count up and down. Kept after a restart by default.

fields.name: The variable's name, like "score".
fields.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch. Empty = the site of whoever started the action.
fields.userId: The viewer's id on their site. Empty = the viewer who started the action, or the one found by user name.
fields.userName: The viewer's chat name, like "kris". Used to find the viewer when you give no id.
fields.mode: Value = save exactly what you type. Increment = add to the current number. Decrement = subtract from it.
fields.value: With Value: what to save. With Increment/Decrement: how much to add or subtract (empty = 1).
fields.persisted: Tick to keep it after Cuebot restarts. Untick for a temporary value that vanishes when Cuebot closes.
fields.autoType: Tick so numbers and true/false are stored as real numbers/yes-no values and not plain text.
fields.storeIn: Optional. A variable to also receive the new value, without % signs, so you can use %name% in the next steps.

desktop.getClipboard.description: Reads the text you last copied (Ctrl+C) and saves it in a variable. Handy for turning a copied link into a chat message.

fields.destination: The variable that receives the copied text, without % signs. The default clipboardText means you use %clipboardText%.

variables.clipboardText: The copied text (the variable name can be changed in the settings)
variables.clipboardTextFound: True if there was text on the clipboard

input.keyboardPress.description: Presses keys on your keyboard for you, as if you typed them, in whatever program is in front. Good for triggering another program's shortcut.

fields.keys: A shortcut like "Ctrl+Shift+F1". For several in a row, separate them with commas, like "Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V". On Linux the desktop may ask for permission once.
fields.delay: How many milliseconds to wait between shortcuts when you list several. 1000 = 1 second.

core.runProgram.description: Starts a program or opens a file on your computer, like a script or another tool. It can wait until the program ends and even collect what it prints.

fields.path: The program or file to open, with its full location, like C:\Tools\clip.exe or /usr/bin/notify-send.
fields.arguments: Extra words to give the program, like "--fast". Empty is fine for most programs.
fields.workingDirectory: The folder the program starts in. Empty = the default. Most people can leave this alone.
fields.wait: Tick to wait for the program to finish before the next step. Unticked, Cuebot goes on straight away.
fields.waitSeconds: With "Wait for exit": give up waiting after this many seconds. 0 = wait as long as it takes.
fields.captureOutput: Tick to save the lines the program prints in %output1%, %output2% and so on. Only works together with "Wait for exit".
fields.environment: Extra settings for the program, one per line as NAME=value. Most people leave this empty.

variables.exitCode: The number the program ended with (0 usually means it went fine). Only after waiting.
variables.timedOut: True if you stopped waiting because the time ran out. Only after waiting.
variables.output1: The first line the program printed (output2 is the second). Only with capture output.
variables.outputCount: How many lines the program printed. Only with capture output.

desktop.setClipboard.description: Puts text on your clipboard, so you can paste it with Ctrl+V. Handy to copy a link or a viewer's message.

fields.text: The text to copy. You can use %variables%, like %message%.

core.setWatcherState.description: Turns a watcher or a followed file on, off or flips it. Watchers are made on the Watchers page. Turn one off if you do not need it right now.

fields.watcher: The name of the watcher or followed file, exactly as on the Watchers page.
fields.state: Enable turns it on. Disable turns it off. Toggle switches it to the opposite.

desktop.showNotification.description: Shows a small pop-up message on your computer screen, only for you, not your viewers. Good as a private reminder. Click it to start an action with the "Toast notification clicked" trigger.

fields.title: The bold line at the top of the pop-up. The default is Cuebot.
fields.message: The text of the pop-up. You can use %variables%.
fields.icon: Optional. The location of a small picture file to show next to the text.
fields.id: Optional. A name you make up so the "Toast notification clicked" trigger can tell which pop-up was clicked.
fields.duration: How many seconds the pop-up stays on screen. From 1 to 120.
fields.target: Auto = your system's notifications where possible, else Cuebot's own pop-up. In-app = always Cuebot's own. System = your system's.

variables.notificationShownWith: Which way the pop-up was shown

core.deleteFile.description: Deletes a file from your computer. Be careful: it is removed for good, not sent to the recycle bin.

fields.path: The file's full location on your computer, like C:\Stream\old.txt.
fields.failIfMissing: Tick to get an error if the file is not there. Unticked, nothing happens when it is missing.

variables.fileDeleted: True if the file existed and was deleted

core.fileExists.description: Checks if a file or folder exists on your computer, then runs the True steps if it does or the False steps if it does not.

fields.path: The full location to look for, like C:\Stream\score.txt.
fields.kind: File = only count files. Folder = only count folders. Either = count both.

core.readFile.description: Reads a whole text file and saves everything in it in a variable. Good for showing text another program wrote, like a song title file.

fields.path: The file's full location on your computer, like C:\Stream\song.txt.
fields.variable: The variable that receives the text, without % signs. The default fileContent means you use %fileContent%.

variables.fileContent: All the text in the file (the variable name can be changed in the settings)

core.readLines.description: Reads a text file line by line. Every line gets its own variable: line0 is the first line, line1 the second, and so on.

fields.path: The file's full location on your computer, like C:\Stream\list.txt.
fields.variable: The start of the variable names, without % signs. With the default line you get %line0%, %line1% and so on.
fields.parseVariables: Tick to replace any %variables% written inside the file with their values.
fields.autoType: Tick so a line that holds a number is stored as a real number. Untick if unsure.

variables.lineCount: How many lines the file has
variables.line0: The first line (line1 is the second, and so on; the start of the name can be changed)
variables.fileFound: True if the file was found

core.readRandomLine.description: Picks a random line from a text file and saves it in a variable. Great for a list of jokes, quotes or ideas that you keep in a plain file.

fields.path: The file's full location on your computer, like C:\Stream\jokes.txt.
fields.variable: The variable that receives the line, without % signs. The default randomLine means you use %randomLine%.
fields.skipEmpty: Tick to never pick an empty line.
fields.count: How many different lines to pick. With more than 1, the extra ones go in randomLine1, randomLine2, and so on.
fields.parseVariables: Tick to replace any %variables% written inside the line with their values.
fields.autoType: Tick so a line that holds a number is stored as a real number. Untick if unsure.

variables.randomLine: The picked line (the variable name can be changed in the settings)
variables.lineNumber: Which line of the file it was, starting at 1
variables.lineCount: How many lines the file could choose from
variables.fileFound: True if the file was found

core.readSpecificLine.description: Reads one chosen line of a text file, for example line 3, and saves it in a variable.

fields.path: The file's full location on your computer, like C:\Stream\list.txt.
fields.variable: The variable that receives the line, without % signs. The default line means you use %line%.
fields.lineNumber: Which line to read. 1 = the first line. If the file is shorter, you get an empty value.
fields.parseVariables: Tick to replace any %variables% written inside the line with their values.
fields.autoType: Tick so a line that holds a number is stored as a real number. Untick if unsure.

variables.line: The line that was read (the variable name can be changed in the settings)
variables.lineCount: How many lines the file has
variables.fileFound: True if the file was found

core.writeFile.description: Writes text into a file on your computer, adding to the end or replacing everything. Good for feeding a text source in OBS, like a follower goal.

fields.path: The file's full location, like C:\Stream\goal.txt. Cuebot creates the file if it is missing.
fields.content: The text to write. You can use %variables%, like "Latest follower: %user%".
fields.mode: Append = add to the end of the file. Overwrite = erase the file and write only this text.
fields.newLine: Tick to finish the text with a line break, so the next write starts on a new line.
fields.createFolders: Tick to create the folders on the way if they do not exist yet.

code.csharp.description: For advanced users: runs a small program written in C# (a programming language). Beginners can skip it, because the other steps do the same things without code.

fields.code: The C# program. It runs inside Cuebot with full access to your computer, so only use code you trust. Beginners: use the normal steps instead.
fields.timeoutSeconds: Stop the code after this many seconds so it cannot get stuck. 0 = no limit.
fields.name: Optional. A name so other code or "Run C# method" can call a method of this code. Most people leave it empty.
fields.description: Optional note for yourself about what this code does.
fields.precompile: Tick to prepare the code when Cuebot starts instead of the first time it runs. For advanced users only.
fields.delayedStart: With "Precompile": wait until Cuebot has finished starting and is connected before preparing the code.
fields.saveResult: Tick to save the code's yes/no answer in a variable and always carry on. Unticked, a "no" (false) stops the action.
fields.resultVariable: The variable that receives the answer when "Save result" is ticked, without % signs.
fields.references: Extra program files (.dll) the code needs, one full location per line. Most code needs none.

code.csharpMethod.description: For advanced users: calls a ready-made C# method that you wrote in a "C# code" step. Beginners can skip it; the normal steps do the same jobs without code.

fields.codeName: The "Code name" you gave a C# code step, or the name of its action.
fields.method: The name of the method to call. It needs no inputs and gives back yes/no or nothing. The default is Execute.
fields.timeoutSeconds: Stop the code after this many seconds so it cannot get stuck. 0 = no limit.
fields.saveResult: Tick to save the code's yes/no answer in a variable and always carry on. Unticked, a "no" (false) stops the action.
fields.resultVariable: The variable that receives the answer when "Save result" is ticked, without % signs.

code.python.description: For advanced users: runs a small program written in Python (a programming language). Beginners can skip it, because the other steps do the same things without code.

fields.code: The Python program. It runs with full access to your computer, so only use code you trust. Python is installed the first time one runs. Beginners: use the normal steps instead.
fields.timeoutSeconds: Stop the code after this many seconds so it cannot get stuck. 0 = no limit.

core.jsonCount.description: Counts the items in a list inside JSON, a common way web services send data. Mostly used after a "Call a web address" step. Beginners rarely need it.

fields.argument: The variable that holds the data, like httpResponse. Empty = use the text in the JSON box instead.
fields.json: The JSON text itself, like [1,2,3]. Ignored when the first box (Read from variable) is filled in.
fields.path: Where the list is inside the data. $ = the whole thing. $.data = the list called data.
fields.variable: The variable that receives the count, without % signs. The default jsonCount means you use %jsonCount%.

variables.jsonCount: How many items the list has (the variable name can be changed in the settings)
variables.jsonFound: True if the place in the data was found

core.jsonGetValue.description: Picks one value out of JSON, a common way web services send data, and saves it in a variable. Mostly used after a "Call a web address" step. Beginners rarely need it.

fields.argument: The variable that holds the data, like httpResponse. Empty = use the text in the JSON box instead.
fields.json: The JSON text itself, like {"name":"Kris"}. Ignored when the first box (Read from variable) is filled in.
fields.path: Where the value is inside the data. $.name = the item called name. $.data[0].name = the name of the first entry in data.
fields.variable: The variable that receives the value, without % signs. The default jsonValue means you use %jsonValue%.

variables.jsonValue: The value that was found (the variable name can be changed in the settings)
variables.jsonFound: True if the place in the data was found

timers.getState.description: Looks up a timer from the Timers page and tells you if it is on, how often it runs and how long until it goes off next.

fields.timer: The timer's name, exactly as on the Timers page. The default %timerName% is the timer that started this action.

variables.timerEnabled: True if the timer is on
variables.timerInterval: How many seconds the timer waits between runs
variables.timerSecondsRemaining: Seconds until it goes off next (-1 if it is not counting down)
variables.timerChatLines: How many chat messages came in since it last ran

timers.setState.description: Turns a timer from the Timers page on, off or flips it, and can change how often it runs. Handy to speed up reminders when chat is busy. Not saved after a restart.

fields.timer: The timer's name, exactly as on the Timers page.
fields.state: Enable turns it on. Disable turns it off. Toggle switches it to the opposite. No change leaves it as it is.
fields.interval: A new wait between runs in whole seconds, like 600 for 10 minutes. Empty keeps the current time.

groups.addUser.description: Puts a viewer into a group of viewers, like "VIPs". Good for rewarding someone who did something special. Groups are lists you can use in commands and points.

fields.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch. The default %platform% means whoever started the action.
fields.user: The viewer's chat name. The default %user% means whoever started the action.
fields.userId: The viewer's id on their site. If known it is used first, otherwise the name is used. The default is whoever started the action.
fields.create: Tick to create the group if it does not exist yet. Unticked, a missing group gives an error.

variables.groupUserAdded: True if they were added, false if they were already in the group

groups.clear.description: Takes every viewer out of a group but keeps the group itself. Good for starting over, like emptying a "Giveaway winners" list.

fields.group: The group's name, like "Giveaway winners". A wrong name gives an error.

variables.groupUsersRemoved: How many viewers were taken out

groups.removeUser.description: Takes a viewer out of a group of viewers.

fields.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch. The default %platform% means whoever started the action.
fields.user: The viewer's chat name. The default %user% means whoever started the action.
fields.userId: The viewer's id on their site. If known it is used first, otherwise the name is used. The default is whoever started the action.

variables.groupUserRemoved: True if they were removed, false if they were not in the group

groups.userInGroup.description: Checks if a viewer is in a group, then runs the True steps if yes or the False steps if no. Example: only VIPs may use a command.

fields.platform: The site the viewer is on, like twitch. The default %platform% means whoever started the action.
fields.user: The viewer's chat name. The default %user% means whoever started the action.
fields.userId: The viewer's id on their site. If known it is used first, otherwise the name is used. The default is whoever started the action.
fields.argument: The variable that receives the answer (true or false), without % signs. The default inGroup means you use %inGroup%.

variables.inGroup: True if the viewer is in the group (the variable name can be changed in the settings)

users.addRandomPresentUser.description: Picks one random viewer who chatted recently and saves their name in variables. Great for "a random viewer wins" or "shout-out someone" actions.

fields.platform: Only pick viewers from this site. All means any site.
fields.argument: The start of the variable names, without % signs. The default randomUser gives %randomUser% (their name), %randomUserId% and more.
fields.excludeCaller: Tick so the viewer who started the action cannot be picked.

variables.randomUser: The picked viewer's display name (the start of the name can be changed in the settings)
variables.randomUserFound: True if someone could be picked

users.resetFirstWords.description: Forgets who has already chatted, so the "First words" trigger can welcome everyone again. It also resets by itself when you go live, unless switched off.

fields.platform: Only forget viewers on this site. All means every site.

commands.getGroupState.description: Checks a group of chat commands and tells you if all, none or some are turned on. Command groups are made on the Commands page.

fields.group: The command group's name from the Commands page.

variables.commandGroupState: 0 = all are off, 1 = all are on, 2 = some on and some off
variables.commandGroupEnabled: True if the group has commands and all are on
variables.commandGroupCount: How many commands are in the group

commands.getState.description: Checks if one chat command is turned on, and how many times it has been used. Pair it with an If step to react.

fields.command: The command's name from the Commands page. The default %commandName% is the command that started this action.

variables.commandEnabled: True if the command is on
variables.commandCounter: How many times the command has been used

commands.getCommands.description: Makes a ready list of your chat commands as text, like "!hello, !discord, !uptime". Good for a !commands reply.

fields.argument: The start of the variable names, without % signs. The default commands gives %commands% (the text), %commandsList% and %commandsCount%.
fields.group: Only list commands of this command group. Empty or All = every group.
fields.show: First alias = each command's first name. All aliases = every name a command answers to. Names = the name you gave it.
fields.separator: What goes between the commands, like a comma and a space.
fields.includeDisabled: Tick to also list commands that are turned off.
fields.includeAll: Tick to also list commands that are set to be left out of the list.
fields.onlyPermitted: Tick to list only the commands the viewer who started the action is allowed to use.

variables.commands: The commands as one line of text (the variable name can be changed in the settings)

commands.resetCounters.description: Sets a command's use counter back to zero, and/or the counters of single viewers. Useful for a "counter" command you want to restart.

fields.command: The command's name from the Commands page. The default %commandName% is the command that started this action.
fields.reset: Counter = the total count. User counters = the counts of single viewers. Both = both.
fields.platform: The site of the viewer, when you reset just one viewer. The default %platform% is whoever started the action.
fields.user: The id of the one viewer to reset. Empty = reset every viewer's counter.

commands.setGroupState.description: Turns all chat commands of a command group on or off, or flips them. Good for switching a whole set at once, like game commands.

fields.group: The command group's name from the Commands page.
fields.state: Enable turns them on. Disable turns them off. Toggle turns all on unless they already are, then turns them off.

commands.setState.description: Turns one chat command on or off, or flips it. Good for a command that should only work during part of the stream.

fields.command: The command's name from the Commands page. The default %commandName% is the command that started this action.
fields.state: Enable turns it on. Disable turns it off. Toggle switches it to the opposite.

variables.commandEnabled: True if the command is on now
